headline: Approved $1,400 for Gatehouse interior cleaning and $24,713 for Seventh Street Bridge design and permitting
summary: The Mine Falls Park Trail Committee approved spending up to $1,400 to clean the interior of the Gatehouse and approved a $24,713 proposal from Hoyle Tanner for design and permitting work on the Seventh Street Bridge. The committee also discussed the Gatehouse structural engineer's report, wildlife issues at the Gatehouse, the proposed new bridge, Whipple Street Bridge priorities, Trail Day projects, and open issues including motorized bikes, bike speeding signage, and encampments.
decisions: Approved a budget not to exceed $1,400 for cleaning the interior of the Gatehouse, including interior windows.
Approved the Hoyle Tanner proposal of approximately $24,713 for Seventh Street Bridge design and permitting.

plain_text:
🌲 Mine Falls Park Trail Committee 
Meeting Minutes — October 5, 2026 
Call to Order 
Steve — 7:00 PM 
Meeting Adjourned 
8:05 PM — Motion: Andrew / Second: Lon 
Attendees: Kamal Masand, Dave Silva, Ben Davis, Sherry Dufzy, Mike Silva, Justin Hoprich, Steve Kenney, Bryan Conant, 
Natalie Lucci, Andrew Lucci, Paula Lochhead, Lon Hochberger, Kimberly Gryslik. 
Guests: Molly Stark and Joseph Peitz. 
1. Approval of Previous Meeting Minutes 
● The minutes of the previous meeting were presented with approval. 
● A correction was identified in Section 2.64 involving the spelling. 
● Motion: Justin made a motion to approve the previous meeting minutes as amended. Paula seconded the 
motion. The meeting then proceeded to the regular agenda. 
2. Guests 
● Guests were welcomed and invited to introduce themselves. 
● Joe: Joe identified himself as an interested citizen of Nashua. 
● Molly: Learned about the meeting through a Facebook post, lives near the park, regularly used the park, and 
attended to learn more about the committee and its work. 
3. Parks Department Report 
● Bryan Conant, Park Superintendent, provided updates on current Park matters. 
Gatehouse — Structural Engineer Report 
● The structural engineer's report for the Gatehouse has not yet been received. 
● Bryan stated that the report was in progress and expressed hope that it would be available well before the 
October 22 Board of Public Works meeting so it could be brought forward for discussion. 
Gatehouse — Interior Cleaning 
● Bryan met with Stratus Cleaning regarding cleaning the interior of the Gatehouse. The proposed work would 
consist of vacuuming and dusting rather than power-washing. 
● Stratus Cleaning provided a quote of $1,400. Bryan noted that the company had recently performed satisfactory 
cleaning work at Holman Stadium. 
● The committee discussed the importance of avoiding exterior power-washing because of the potential for 
damage to the building and mortar. 
● Discussion also addressed cleaning products, access to interior windows, supervision while the work is 
performed, and the likelihood that animal activity could cause the interior to become soiled again. 
● Motion: Approve a budget not to exceed $1,400 for cleaning the interior of the Gatehouse, including the interior 
windows. 
● Vote: The motion passed without opposition. 
Gatehouse — Animal/Wildlife Concerns
● Members discussed evidence of animal activity and waste inside the Gatehouse. Possible sources included mice, 
rats, and bats. 
● Bryan explained that pest-control vendors are used in other city buildings and that a vendor could potentially be 
engaged for the Gatehouse. 
● Members raised concerns about chemical bait and the possibility of secondary impacts on wildlife through the 
food chain, particularly because of the Gatehouse's location near the water. 
● Alternatives discussed included traps, identifying entry points, and installing mesh or similar barriers. 
● Consensus: Proceed first with cleaning, evaluate conditions afterward, and revisit wildlife-control measures, as 
necessary. 
4. New Bridge 
● Bryan reported that there was no new information regarding the proposed new bridge. 
● As discussed previously, the bridge is expected to be located on the east/back side of the soccer and softball field 
complex and provide access toward the tannery area once that area is developed. 
● Steve reported that Matt Sullivan was unable to attend because of a conflict but had committed to attending the 
next meeting. 
●  Steve had discussed with him the desirability of establishing a consistent bridge design or template for future 
bridge replacements throughout the park. The bridge behind South High School was mentioned as a possible 
model, while recognizing that a larger river crossing may require a different design. 
5. Seventh Street Bridge 
● Hoyle Tanner had inspected the Seventh Street Bridge. The engineering review reflected concerns about the 
existing floor construction and materials and indicated that these conditions would continue to create issues. 
● Hoyle Tanner can prepare engineering design, permitting, bid specifications, and bid documents for the project. 
● Bryan reported a proposal of approximately $24,713 for the design and permitting phase. Hoyle Tanner was also 
involved with the bridge replacement behind South High School and the Whipple Street Bridge project. 
● Members discussed the proposal in the context of other capital needs, including the Gatehouse and Whipple 
Street Bridge. 
● It was clarified that the $24,713 amount is for the planning/design and permitting work and is not the cost of 
repairing or replacing the Seventh Street Bridge.  
● Motion to approve 24713 was made and seconded. Motion Passed.  
6. Whipple Street Bridge / Capital Priorities 
● The committee briefly discussed the Whipple Street Bridge and competing capital priorities. 
● Bryan did not have an exact schedule for the Whipple Street project but indicated that it was being discussed 
and evaluated. 
● Members also discussed preserving or earmarking available funding for the Gatehouse while awaiting the 
information needed to move that project forward. 
Gatehouse Cleaning Authorize up to $1,400 for interior cleaning, including 
interior windows. 
Approved  
Gatehouse Structural 
Report 
Await structural engineer’s report for future discussion. Pending. 
Gatehouse Wildlife Clean first, evaluate conditions and entry points, then 
revisit control measures. 
Follow-up needed.
Bridge Planning Discuss a consistent bridge design/template with Matt 
Sullivan at a future meeting. 
Pending. 
Seventh Street Bridge Hoyle Tanner proposal of approximately $24,713 for 
design/permitting discussed. 
Approved  
📘 Facebook: As per Natalie, we have 6,000 followers on Facebook. 
🍂 Trail Day Projects 
• Painting (subject to weather) 
• Clean brushes 
• Trim brushes 
• Clean debris around trees 
• Whipple Street painting 
• Fix the retaining wall 
• Visit the Island area 
💬 Open Discussion 
● 🛵 Motorized Bikes: The committee discussed how to enforce the rules on motorized bikes on 
the trails. 
● 🚴 Bike Speeding: It was decided that board members will come up with creative signage ideas to 
address the bike speeding issue. Input from community members will also be welcomed. 
● ⛺ Encampments: Steve suggested conducting a survey via Facebook about the encampment 
issue, which will help the committee gauge the pulse of the Nashua community.
